mainTopic: How an ox becomes a מועד through patterns of victims, days, dates and triggers, and liability when an ox of הקדש or of a גוי is involved.
overview: The amud opens with four linked questions about how a goring ox becomes a מועד. In each one, a single goring could complete either a 'same type' group of three or a 'mixed' group of three. Two of the questions are about the species of the victims, and two are about days of the week. The גמרא cannot decide them, and they end in תיקו. Next, an ox that gores on a date that moves forward one day each month is tied to the dispute of רב and שמואל about a woman's וסת. רבא then rules that an ox that gores three times after hearing a שופר becomes a מועד for שופרות, even though the first goring might have been just a fright. A new משנה follows: when הקדש is involved there is no payment, a Jew's ox that gores a גוי's ox is פטור, and a גוי's ox that gores a Jew's ox pays full damages. The גמרא says the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, who makes an ordinary ox that harms הקדש pay in full even as a תם. A קל וחומר explanation fails because of דיו, so ריש לקיש explains that full damages is the default and 'רעהו' only limits the half-damage discount of a תם.

steps.title: Three oxen, then a donkey and a camel
steps.stepSummary: An ox gored three oxen and then a donkey and a camel. Does the last ox count toward a mixed group that makes it מועד for all species?
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox gored an ox, another ox and a third ox, and then a donkey and a camel. What is the law? Do we group the last ox with the earlier oxen, so the ox is still מועד only for oxen and not for other kinds of animals? Or do we group that last ox with the donkey and the camel, so the ox becomes מועד for every kind of animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question: the ox gored three oxen in a row and then a donkey and a camel. Which group does the third ox belong to?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three gorings make an ox מועד. The third ox can be counted two ways. With the other two oxen, it makes three oxen, so the ox is מועד only for oxen. With the donkey and camel, it makes three different species, so the ox is מועד for all species. The question is whether one goring can count in both groups, or which group it belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (opens a question)
the last one
we throw it in with, we group it with
it became מועד (forewarned)
or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
all the species

steps.confusionAlert: There are not five separate counts here. The whole question is about one goring, the third ox, and which group of three it completes.

phrases.english: An ox, an ox, and an ox,
phrases.notes: These are the three oxen our ox gored, one after another.

phrases.english: then a donkey and a camel: what is the law?
This last ox:
do we group it with the oxen,
so that it is still only for oxen that it became forewarned,
but for anything else it did not become forewarned;
or perhaps this last ox
we group with the donkey and the camel,
and it became forewarned for all species?

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹר, שׁוֹר וָשׁוֹר, חֲמוֹר וְגָמָל, מַהוּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the last ox in the series counted with the oxen, so the ox is מועד for oxen only, or with the donkey and camel, so it is מועד for all species?

steps.title: A donkey and a camel, then three oxen
steps.stepSummary: This is the reverse order: a donkey and a camel first, then three oxen. Does the first ox complete the mixed group, or does it belong with the oxen that come after it?
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox gored a donkey and a camel, and then an ox, another ox and a third ox. What is the law? Do we group the first ox with the donkey and the camel, so the ox is מועד for every kind of animal? Or do we group it with the oxen that came after it, so it is still מועד only for oxen and not for other kinds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question with the order flipped. Now the shared goring is the first ox, which comes right after the donkey and camel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ox could complete a group of three different species: donkey, camel, ox. Or it could be the first of three oxen. Asking about both orders checks whether it matters if the shared goring comes at the start or the end of the oxen series.

keyTerms.meaning: the first one
a different species

phrases.aramaic: חֲמוֹר וְגָמָל, שׁוֹר, שׁוֹר וָשׁוֹר, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: A donkey and a camel, then an ox, an ox, and an ox: what is the law?
This first ox:
do we group it with the donkey and the camel,
so that it became forewarned for all species;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא בָּתַר שְׁווֹרִים שָׁדֵינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps we group it with the oxen,
so that it is still only for oxen that it became forewarned,
but for another species it did not become forewarned?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמוֹר וְגָמָל, שׁוֹר, שׁוֹר וָשׁוֹר, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the mirror image of step 1. The order is reversed, so the shared goring is now the first ox instead of the last.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the first ox counted with the donkey and camel, so the ox is מועד for all species, or with the following oxen, so it is מועד for oxen only?

steps.title: Three שבת gorings, then Sunday and Monday
steps.stepSummary: The same question, now about days of the week. Does the last שבת goring count with the שבת series, or with Sunday and Monday to make three days in a row?
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox gored on שבת, on the next שבת, and on the next שבת, and then on Sunday and on Monday. What is the law? Do we group the last שבת with the earlier שבתות, so the ox is still מועד only for שבת and not for weekdays? Or do we group it with Sunday and Monday, so the ox becomes מועד for every day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the same question from types of animals to days of the week. The goring on the third שבת could belong to either of two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three gorings on three שבתות would make the ox מועד only for שבת. But the last שבת is followed right away by Sunday and Monday, which makes three days in a row and would make the ox מועד for all days. The puzzle about the shared goring is exactly the same as in steps 1 and 2.

keyTerms.meaning: the last one (feminine form, because it refers to שבת)
the first day of the week, Sunday
the second day of the week, Monday
weekdays
all the days

phrases.english: Shabbos, Shabbos, and Shabbos,
phrases.notes: He means three שבתות in a row, one goring each week.

phrases.english: then Sunday and Monday: what is the law?
This last Shabbos:
is it with the Shabbos gorings that we group it,
so that it is still only for Shabbos that it became forewarned,
but for weekdays it did not become forewarned;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא בָּתַר אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת וְשֵׁנִי בְּשַׁבָּת שָׁדֵינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps we group it with Sunday and Monday,
and it became forewarned for all days?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת, אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת וְשֵׁנִי בְּשַׁבָּת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This applies the same grouping question from steps 1 and 2 to time (days of the week) instead of the species of the victims.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the last שבת goring counted with the earlier שבתות, so the ox is מועד for שבת only, or with Sunday and Monday, so it is מועד for every day?

steps.title: Thursday, Friday, שבת, then two more שבתות
steps.stepSummary: The reverse of the previous question. The ox gores on Thursday, Friday and שבת, then on the next two שבתות. Does the first שבת join Thursday and Friday (three days in a row), or does it join the later שבתות (three שבתות)?
steps.simpleTranslation: If an ox gored on Thursday, Friday and שבת, and then on the next שבת and the שבת after that, what is the law? Do we group this first שבת with Thursday and Friday, so the ox becomes a מועד for every day? Or perhaps we group this first שבת with the other שבתות, so it is a מועד only for שבתות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, but with the order flipped. Now the shared שבת comes first instead of last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One goring, the first שבת, could finish two different patterns. If it joins Thursday and Friday, we have three days in a row and the ox is a מועד every day. If it joins the next two שבתות, we have three שבתות and the ox is a מועד only on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Thursday (literally 'the fifth day of the week')
Friday (literally 'the eve of שבת')
the first one (feminine form, because it refers to שבת)

phrases.english: If an ox gored on Thursday, Friday, and Shabbat,
and then the next Shabbat and the Shabbat after that, what is the law?
This first Shabbat:

phrases.aramaic: בָּתַר חֲמִישִׁי בְּשַׁבָּת וְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שָׁדֵינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: do we group it together with Thursday and Friday,
so the ox became a מועד for all days?
Or perhaps this first Shabbat
is grouped together with the other Shabbatot,
so the ox is a מועד only for Shabbatot?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִישִׁי בְּשַׁבָּת וְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverse order of step 3, just as step 2 reversed step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the first, shared שבת belong to the series of days in a row before it, or to the series of שבתות after it?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends this whole set of questions with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand. The questions remain unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes all the questions about mixed patterns (steps 1-4) without deciding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found that tells us whether a shared goring joins the pattern before it or the pattern after it. So all four cases, the animal cases and the day cases, are left as open doubts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it stand': the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: In all four cases, one goring could finish two different patterns. The גמרא could not decide which pattern it belongs to, so the questions end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let these questions stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of questions from steps 1-4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about overlapping patterns are left undecided.

steps.title: An ox goring on the 15th, 16th and 17th of three months
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the ox gores one day later in each month. The גמרא says this depends on a dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an ox gored on the 15th of one month, the 16th of the next month, and the 17th of the month after that, this is the dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new kind of pattern: the date moves forward by one day each month. It tells us the answer depends on an argument between רב and שמואל, and the next step shows us that argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no single fixed date. The pattern is 'one day later each time.' The question is whether three such gorings already count as a pattern, or whether more are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: gored
a dispute

phrases.aramaic: נָגַח שׁוֹר יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּחוֹדֶשׁ זֶה,
phrases.english: If an ox gored on the fifteenth day of this month,
and on the sixteenth day of the next month,
and on the seventeenth day of the month after that,
it is the dispute between Rav and Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו: a pattern that moves forward each month
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that gores on a date that moves forward one day each month depends on the dispute of רב and שמואל.

steps.title: The source: רב and שמואל on a moving וסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute it was pointing to. A woman sees blood on the 15th, 16th and 17th of three months. רב says she has set a וסת. שמואל says she needs the 'skip' to happen three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: if a woman saw blood on the 15th of one month, the 16th of the next, and the 17th of the month after that, רב says she has set a וסת. שמואל says she has not, until the skip happens three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the dispute about a woman's וסת to show what it meant in the previous step. The same argument applies to the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב counts three sightings as enough to set the pattern. שמואל says the real pattern is the jump of one day, and here there were only two jumps (15 to 16, 16 to 17). So he needs a third jump, meaning a fourth sighting. Applied to the ox, רב would make it a מועד after three gorings, and שמואל would require four.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was stated (introduces an אמוראic teaching)
a woman's set pattern for her period
she established (set)
she does it three times
with a skip (a jump of one day)

steps.whatToRemember: A date that moves forward one day each month: רב says three times sets the pattern. שמואל says the skip itself must happen three times. The same dispute applies to an ox becoming a מועד.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not counting sightings, he is counting skips. Three sightings give only two skips, so he needs one more.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִתְּמַר: רָאֲתָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה,
phrases.english: As it was stated: If a woman saw blood on the fifteenth day of this month,
and on the sixteenth day of the next month,
and on the seventeenth day of the month after that,
Rav says: She has set herself a וסת.
And Shmuel says: Not until she skips three times.
phrases.notes: He means three jumps of one day, so she needs a fourth sighting, on the 18th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the dispute that step 6 pointed to
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: three sightings with a one-day skip set a וסת. שמואל: the skip itself must happen three times.

steps.title: An ox that gores when it hears a shofar
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an ox that gores three times, each time right after hearing a שופר, becomes a מועד for שופר situations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If an ox heard a שופר and gored, heard a שופר and gored, and heard a שופר and gored, it becomes a מועד for שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds one more kind of pattern that can make an ox a מועד. Here the pattern is a sound, not a day or a date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא talked about patterns of days, like goring every שבת. רבא says a repeated trigger also counts: three gorings after a שופר make the ox a מועד for whenever it hears a שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: A ram's horn that is blown and makes a loud sound
It gored (attacked with its horns)
An ox with a proven habit of damaging. Its owner pays full damages
Plural of שופר: times when a שופר is blown

steps.confusionAlert: The ox becomes a מועד for שופר situations only. It is not a מועד for every goring.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If it heard the sound of a shofar and gored,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ox; the גמרא leaves the word out.

phrases.english: again the sound of a shofar and it gored,
and again the sound of a shofar and it gored –
it becomes forewarned for shofar sounds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר וְנָגַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the questions about species and days of the week end with תיקו, and the moving-date case is tied to the רב/שמואל dispute, רבא brings a new kind of pattern: a repeated trigger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three gorings, each after hearing a שופר, make the ox a מועד for שופר situations.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since three gorings in a clear pattern should obviously count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא's rule needs to be said at all. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three gorings in the same situation seems like a plain case of a habit. So the גמרא wants to know what new thing רבא is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. This asks why a statement was needed at all

phrases.english: Isn't this obvious?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבא's ruling in step 8 needed to be said.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea is רבא teaching, if three gorings in one situation obviously make a habit?

steps.title: The first goring was not just from fright
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the first goring happened only because the ox got scared, so it would not count. רבא teaches that it does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the first time the שופר just startled the ox, so that goring should not count. רבא teaches us that it does count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. It shows the mistake רבא's rule is coming to prevent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sudden loud sound can scare an animal one time, so the first goring might seem like a one-time accident and not a habit. Since the ox kept goring every time it heard a שופר, the first goring is part of the pattern too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a wrong idea that the teaching comes to rule out
A scare or fright
Merely, just
It teaches us. This introduces the real point of a statement

steps.whatToRemember: An ox can become a מועד for a repeated trigger like a שופר. Even the first goring counts toward the three, because we do not write it off as a one-time fright.

phrases.english: You might have said:
that first shofar –
it was merely a fright that seized it;
so he teaches us that it does count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'isn't it obvious' question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: points to a reasonable mistake that the ruling comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first goring came only from a sudden fright, so it should not count toward making the ox a מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three gorings count, the first one included, so the ox is a מועד for שופרות.

steps.title: משנה: No payment when an ox of הקדש is involved
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a regular ox gores an ox of הקדש, or an ox of הקדש gores a regular ox, the owner is פטור. The source is the פסוק 'the ox of his fellow'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If an ox of a Jew gored an ox of הקדש, or an ox of הקדש gored a regular ox, the owner is פטור. This is because the פסוק says 'the ox of his fellow', and not an ox of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: who owns the oxen. It rules that when הקדש owns one of the oxen, no one pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about 'the ox of his fellow', meaning an ox that belongs to a person. An ox of הקדש belongs to the בית המקדש, not to a 'fellow'. So there is no payment, whether the הקדש ox did the goring or was the one gored.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה
Property set aside for the בית המקדש
A regular person, or property that is not holy
Exempt, does not have to pay
'The ox of his fellow.' The words in the פסוק that teach this law

steps.confusionAlert: The exemption works in both directions: when the הקדש ox gores, and when the הקדש ox is gored.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: An ox of a Jew that gored a consecrated ox,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט –
phrases.english: and a consecrated ox that gored an ordinary person's ox –
is exempt, as it is stated:
"the ox of his fellow" –
and not a consecrated ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic changes from how an ox becomes a מועד to who owns the oxen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When an ox of הקדש gores or is gored, there is no liability, because the פסוק says 'שׁוֹר רֵעֵהוּ'.

steps.title: משנה: When a Jew's ox and a גוי's ox gore each other
steps.stepSummary: A Jew's ox that gores a גוי's ox: the owner is פטור. A גוי's ox that gores a Jew's ox: full damages are paid, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jew's ox gored a גוי's ox, the owner is פטור. But if a גוי's ox gored a Jew's ox, the owner pays full damages, whether his ox is a תם or a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another ownership case: a Jew's ox and a גוי's ox. Here, unlike הקדש, the two directions get different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the הקדש case, both directions were פטור. Here they split: in one direction the owner pays nothing, and in the other he pays full damages even for a תם, which usually pays only half. The משנה states the rule without a reason; the גמרא will discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
An ox with no habit of goring. Usually its owner pays half damages
Full damages

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two ownership rules: with הקדש, there is no payment in either direction. With a גוי, a Jew's ox goring a גוי's ox is פטור, while a גוי's ox goring a Jew's ox pays full damages, even as a תם.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the usual rule that a תם pays half. Here the משנה says full damages, even for a תם.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שֶׁל גּוֹי – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: An ox of a Jew that gored the ox of a gentile – the owner is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל גּוֹי שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: But an ox of a gentile that gored the ox of a Jew –
whether it is innocuous or forewarned,
he pays the full damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שֶׁל גּוֹי – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second ownership case. This time the ruling depends on which ox did the goring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew's ox that gores a גוי's ox is פטור. A גוי's ox that gores a Jew's ox pays full damages, whether it is a תם or a מועד.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן מנסיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. It quotes a ברייתא whose first opinion matches the משנה: both directions of goring involving הקדש are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא says: our משנה is not like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. A ברייתא teaches: if an ordinary ox gores a הקדש ox, or a הקדש ox gores an ordinary ox, there is no payment, because the פסוק says 'the ox of his fellow', and not a הקדש ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by saying it does not match one תנא, רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and this first opinion agrees with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא reads 'רעהו' (his fellow) strictly. הקדש is not 'your fellow', so neither direction of goring is paid. This is exactly what our משנה said, and it sets up the contrast with רבי שמעון בן מנסיא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
As it was taught in a ברייתא
An ordinary ox, owned by a private person
An ox that belongs to the Temple
'The ox of his fellow', the פסוק used to limit damages to oxen of fellow people

phrases.aramaic: גּמ׳ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishna is not in line with Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya,
as it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: An ordinary ox that gored a consecrated ox,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: or a consecrated ox that gored an ordinary ox: exempt,
as it is said: "the ox of his fellow"
and not an ox of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows the view that both directions of goring involving הקדש are פטור, not the view of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא splits the two cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא rules that a הקדש ox goring an ordinary ox is פטור, but an ordinary ox goring a הקדש ox pays full damages, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: a הקדש ox that gored an ordinary ox is פטור. An ordinary ox that gored a הקדש ox pays full damages, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the second opinion, from רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. He treats the two directions differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When הקדש does the damage, nobody pays. When הקדש is the victim, the owner pays in full. He even makes a תם pay full damages, which is stricter than the normal half payment for a תם. This is the opinion our משנה does not follow.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox with no history of goring; normally pays half damages
An ox known to gore; pays full damages
Full damages

steps.confusionAlert: Even a תם pays full damages here, which is not the normal rule. This detail becomes the key problem in step 17.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט – פָּטוּר;
phrases.english: A consecrated ox that gored an ordinary ox: exempt;

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ –
phrases.english: but an ordinary ox that gored a consecrated ox:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין תָּם בֵּין מוּעָד, מְשַׁלֵּם נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם.
phrases.english: whether innocuous or forewarned, the owner pays full damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion in the ברייתא, disagreeing with the first opinion from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הקדש ox that gores is פטור. An ordinary ox that gores a הקדש ox pays full damages, even if it is a תם.

steps.title: How can רבי שמעון split the cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון's reasoning is. If 'רעהו' is meant strictly, both cases should be פטור. If it is not meant strictly, both cases should be חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What does רבי שמעון hold? If 'his fellow' is exact, then even an ordinary ox that gored a הקדש ox should be exempt! And if 'his fellow' is not exact, then even a הקדש ox that gored an ordinary ox should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's split ruling. It argues that one פסוק should give the same result both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'רעהו' either excludes הקדש or it does not. If it excludes הקדש, it should exclude it whether הקדש is the damager or the victim. Either way, a split ruling seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They said; the חכמים in the בית מדרש
What does he hold?
Exact, meant strictly
Not exact, not meant strictly

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: מַאי קָא סָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: They said: What does Rabbi Shimon hold?
If "his fellow" is meant exactly,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁנָּגַח שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ לִיפְּטַר!
phrases.english: then even an ordinary ox that gored a consecrated one should be exempt!
And if "his fellow" is not meant exactly,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ נָמֵי, כִּי נָגַח דְּהֶדְיוֹט לִיחַיַּיב!
phrases.english: then a consecrated ox too, when it gores an ordinary one, should be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מַאי קָא סָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's ruling in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's split between הקדש as damager and הקדש as victim.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single פסוק, 'רעהו', must work the same way in both directions. Either both cases are פטור or both are חייב.

steps.title: A suggested answer: a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון reads 'רעהו' strictly, so a הקדש damager is פטור. He makes an ordinary ox that harmed הקדש liable through a קל וחומר: if harming an ordinary ox brings liability, harming הקדש surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: really he holds 'his fellow' is exact, but an ordinary ox that gores a הקדש ox is liable for another reason. He learns it from a קל וחומר: if an ordinary ox that gores an ordinary ox is liable, then when it gores a הקדש ox, surely it is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to explain רבי שמעון. It is phrased as 'if you will say', which sets up a rejection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'רעהו' really does exclude הקדש, which explains why a הקדש damager is פטור. The liability for harming הקדש comes from a separate source, a קל וחומר from an ordinary victim. So the split is explained by two different sources.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; introduces a suggested answer that is about to be rejected
Really, actually
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
All the more so, surely

phrases.english: And if you will say: really he holds "his fellow" is meant exactly,
but when an ordinary ox gores a consecrated one,
this is the reason it is liable:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר דְּהֶדְיוֹט:
phrases.english: because he derives it by a kal vachomer from an ordinary ox:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁנָּגַח שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: If an ordinary ox that gored an ordinary ox is liable,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נָגַח דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ – לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּמִיחַיַּיב?
phrases.english: when it gores a consecrated ox, is it not all the more so liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate sources: the פסוק explains the פטור, and a קל וחומר explains the חיוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single reading of 'רעהו' must give the same result in both directions.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רעהו' excludes הקדש, but liability for harming הקדש comes from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: The rule of דיו defeats the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. A קל וחומר cannot teach more than its source (דיו). Since a תם that gores an ordinary ox pays only half damages, the קל וחומר could only require half damages, yet רבי שמעון said full damages even for a תם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source! Just as there a תם pays half damages, here too it should pay only half damages!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר answer from step 16 using the rule of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under דיו, a law learned through a קל וחומר cannot be stricter than the case it comes from. The source case, an ordinary ox goring an ordinary ox, has a תם paying only half. So the קל וחומר cannot produce the full payment for a תם that רבי שמעון ruled, and his view is still unexplained.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for a law learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source, and not stricter
There, in the source case
Half damages

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר can never make the new case stricter than its source (דיו). So the קל וחומר cannot explain why רבי שמעון בן מנסיא makes a תם pay full damages to הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule of דיו in action: it limits how far a קל וחומר can reach, and here it blocks the suggested explanation.

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין – לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן!
phrases.english: It is enough for what comes from the kal vachomer to be like its source!
Just as there, an innocuous ox pays half damages,
here too it should be half damages!

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר answer offered in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the קל וחומר as the explanation for רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's full payment by a תם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Because of דיו, the קל וחומר can only produce half damages for a תם, not the full damages רבי שמעון ruled.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Full damages is the default, and the half-damage discount applies only to 'רעהו'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains רבי שמעון בן מנסיא differently. Every ox that damages starts out under the rule of נזק שלם. The word 'רעהו' in the תם verse limits the חצי נזק discount to damage done to another person's ox. So when הקדש is damaged, the owner pays נזק שלם, whether his ox is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ריש לקיש said: In principle, all damages fall under the rule of full payment. When the פסוק specified 'his fellow' regarding a תם, it meant this: only when it harms 'his fellow' does a תם pay half damages. We learn from this that for הקדש, whether the ox is a תם or a מועד, the owner pays full damages.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the קל וחומר explanation, the גמרא brings ריש לקיש's new explanation for why an ordinary ox that gores a הקדש ox pays full damages even as a תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 tried to create liability toward הקדש through a קל וחומר, and that failed because of דיו. ריש לקיש flips the approach. Full payment is the starting point, and 'רעהו' only narrows the half-payment discount of a תם. Since nothing has to be learned from a קל וחומר, the limit of דיו never comes up, and a תם that harms הקדש pays in full.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא (Talmudic scholar) who offers the new explanation of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא
Included in the general rule of paying full damages
Specified or singled out. The פסוק narrowed a rule to a specific case.
Half damages, which is what the owner of a תם normally pays
By inference. We learn something from what the text implies.
An ox with an established habit of goring, whose owner pays full damages

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, the word 'רעהו' does not create liability. It only limits the half-damage discount of a תם. When הקדש is harmed, the default of full damages applies.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 16. There, 'רעהו' was read as limiting liability itself, and liability toward הקדש had to come from a קל וחומר. Here, 'רעהו' only limits the discount. That is why a תם pays full damages to הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation avoids the problem of דיו from Step 17. It shows how the same word in the פסוק can limit either the liability or the discount, depending on how you read it.

phrases.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said:
All were included in the rule of full damages;
when the verse specified for you:
'his fellow' regarding a tam —

phrases.aramaic: רֵעֵהוּ הוּא דְּתָם מְשַׁלֵּם חֲצִי נֶזֶק;
phrases.english: it is only for 'his fellow' that a tam pays half damages;
by inference, for consecrated property —
whether a tam or a mu'ad,
he pays full damages;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the קל וחומר explanation that Step 17 rejected with a new reading of 'רעהו'
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the verse: 'רעהו' limits the half-damage discount, not the liability itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Liability for harming הקדש must come from a קל וחומר, which would be limited by דיו to half damages for a תם
steps.terutzMaskana: Full damages is the default, and 'רעהו' restricts only the חצי נזק discount, so a תם that harms הקדש pays נזק שלם
